'A captain wants eight matching satchel: 'A captain wants eight matching satchel strap sets by morning. I have the leather. I do not have eight pairs of hands. Studio's open, get in there.'
'A clean break. Rest. The next seal will: 'A clean break. Rest. The next seal will not be so quiet.'
'A clerk was robbed last week. The lockb: 'A clerk was robbed last week. The lockbox was empty by morning, but the wax seal on the lid was still warm. Same mark turned up in Shortha and Redhelm the same week.'
'A hand west. I knew it. Guild owes me a: 'A hand west. I knew it. Guild owes me a printer's apology. They won't give it, but they'll pay for the reprint. Take your share now.'
'A rift has opened near the Veilbridge. The discover team flagged a mushroom-thing. Survey it then handle it.'
'A trapper came through with a strip of: 'A trapper came through with a strip of dragonhide off something he didn't kill. He said it was caught on a tree, and the tree was twenty paces inside the hollows. I want to know what's molting in there.'
'All four anchors quiet. For now. The br: 'All four anchors quiet. For now. The bridge holds.'
'Anvil cracked clean through last night. Caravan wants forty bars by dawn and I can't strike a thing. Smelt them at my forge and I'll cool them.'
'Assessor arrives Wednesday. He won't fi: 'Assessor arrives Wednesday. He won't find a thing. You saved the market its license. Take this from the discretionary purse.'
'Assessor's here in eight days. Three br: 'Assessor's here in eight days. Three brokers' books haven't been reconciled in two seasons. I need the numbers honest by the time he opens the ledger.'
'Better prices for the guild! You are a: 'Better prices for the guild! You are a natural. Here, your commission.'
'Boy ran off with a fiddler's daughter. Left me ten bars short on an order due before sundown. Get to the anvil and finish them.'
'Boys have been on hardtack and stew sin: 'Boys have been on hardtack and stew since the thaw. Six weeks. I want squid on the table tonight and I want the foreman to cry a little.'
'Brewer wants fifty battle roots, no scr: 'Brewer wants fifty battle roots, no scraps, by market day. My back row got rabbits. You can plant fast? Good. Take the seed.'
'Buyer comes at first light. I need clea: 'Buyer comes at first light. I need clean samples off the new face, not the rubble pile. Crack a few and bring them back.'
'Buyer rides in three days. I'm twenty h: 'Buyer rides in three days. I'm twenty hides short. Walk the wilds and don't come back with rabbits, I need the heavy stuff.'
'Buyer's at the gate. You earned the bon: 'Buyer's at the gate. You earned the bonus. Stop by the foundry next week if you want steady work.'
'Caravan came in two crates short. Drive: 'Caravan came in two crates short. Drivers swore the seals were intact at the gate. We pulled one off, kept it as evidence.' He slides a wax chip across. Same four lines.
'Caravan leaves Friday. They paid in adv: 'Caravan leaves Friday. They paid in advance for thirty mithril bars. My smith hurt his arm and my apprentice can barely heat copper. Help us out.'
'Caravans hit the gate at sundown tomorr: 'Caravans hit the gate at sundown tomorrow. Apothecary's bone dry. Pull the herbs from the pool grounds and brew through the night.'
'Cave-in took three carts and a week's h: 'Cave-in took three carts and a week's haul. Quota's still due. The vein up top is light but the shaft below it is still good. Help me dig out.'
'Clean job. He'll come back to bare boar: 'Clean job. He'll come back to bare boards and a sleeping dog. Your share is heavier than mine and that's how I like it.'
'Cleaner than expected. Keep watching th: 'Cleaner than expected. Keep watching that bridge.'
'Coat off my wagon between here and the: 'Coat off my wagon between here and the inn. Someone got bold. Find them, take it back, leave a mark they'll remember without leaving a body.'
'Conduit's been spitting since the storm: 'Conduit's been spitting since the storm. If the casing splits, the whole rig goes. Bleed it into the next town's font and come back quick.'
'Crystal lost half its glow between dusk: 'Crystal lost half its glow between dusk and dawn. I don't know if it's drawn or drained. Stand on it and tell me which it feels like.'
'Eastern ranges go under snow in six wee: 'Eastern ranges go under snow in six weeks. I've got two passes to confirm and one ridge unmarked. I need eyes and steady hands. You're both.'
'Every year the same. Booths run out of: 'Every year the same. Booths run out of thread, booths run out of tanned hide, booths run out of patience. You'll wear this badge and you'll run for whoever needs you. Don't take sides. Don't take tips. Take pay at the end.'
'Fifty even and the bark on top. Brewer': 'Fifty even and the bark on top. Brewer's going to pay full. You took my problem and gave me a customer for next season. Take a cut of both.'
'Five stills across five towns, one for: 'Five stills across five towns, one for every year I worked them. Brew a batch at each. Come back if all five come back clean.'
'Foot's the size of a turnip. Thicket's: 'Foot's the size of a turnip. Thicket's a half mile up the hill and I'm not walking it. Pick me a basket and I'll teach you what they're good for.'
'Forty even, sealed clean. Patrol captai: 'Forty even, sealed clean. Patrol captain will sleep easy and so will I. Take the extras.'
'Forty pieces. On time. I won't underbid: 'Forty pieces. On time. I won't underbid again. Take a share. And don't tell my apprentice you stitched faster than she did, it'll wreck her.'
'Found a rib bone on the pantry floor th: 'Found a rib bone on the pantry floor that wasn't there at close. Door was bolted. I'm not going back in until something walks out of it dead.'
'Four ancients. Four seals. The veil is: 'Four ancients. Four seals. The veil is thinning. Start with the cartograph and trace each one back to its anchor.'
'Four passers-by stoned on the south roa: 'Four passers-by stoned on the south road this month. The last one was a merchant I've known twenty years. End her or we close the road for the season.'
'Four runners. That's all I needed. The: 'Four runners. That's all I needed. The other six can carry water. Take the bonus and the day off.'
'Four stalls fined, one warned, one clea: 'Four stalls fined, one warned, one cleared. Take your cut, and a tip from me for not pocketing the difference yourself.'
'Fourteen days they've laid somewhere I: 'Fourteen days they've laid somewhere I can't find, and the dog won't help. My wife thinks it's funny.'
'Frost came two nights ago. Half the tre: 'Frost came two nights ago. Half the trees are gone. The other half I can save if someone works the rows with me starting now.'
'Full delivery. Winteredge owes you a ho: 'Full delivery. Winteredge owes you a hot meal.'
'Goats got in the rows twice this week. I've replanted what I could. Go see what's left and put the new shoots in before the sun cooks them.'
'Guild inspectors hit us Tuesday and hal: 'Guild inspectors hit us Tuesday and half my stalls haven't priced honest in six months. I need someone to buy and sell across the floor and write down who tries what.'
'Guild ordered twelve coats and I cut fo: 'Guild ordered twelve coats and I cut for nine. Three more by the end of the week or my workshop loses its seal. Take the cutting bench. I'll do the stitch.'
'Half is more than I had this morning. T: 'Half is more than I had this morning. Take what you want from the dry store. You earned it twice.'
'Hauled wrong last load and my back went: 'Hauled wrong last load and my back went. Sacks are at the bank, road's down the valley, two trips will do it. Walk fast, the buyer leaves at noon.'
'House bard fell off a barrel and snappe: 'House bard fell off a barrel and snapped his arm. Booking's paid for thirty nights so I'd rather hire you than refund. Play nice and don't sing about politics.'
'I asked around. The seal's a runner's m: 'I asked around. The seal's a runner's mark. They hand off at the alley behind the Shortha southbank. Catch one alive if you can.'
'I been digging this hill since I was tw: 'I been digging this hill since I was twelve. Hit a seam Tuesday that smells like rotted iron and tastes like nothing. I want a second pick on it before I tell the foreman.'
'I bid on a forty piece order thinking I: 'I bid on a forty piece order thinking I'd have two apprentices by now. I have one and she's seasick. Help me work the studio for three days.'
'I left the spit unattended and lost the: 'I left the spit unattended and lost the lot. Crew lands in two hours and they don't pay for cinders. Cook a proper supper.'
'I need someone to head over to the mark: 'I need someone to head over to the market and establish trade with the merchants. A combined explorer and merchant. Think you can handle it?'
'I thought the brine would hold them. It: 'I thought the brine would hold them. It did, but they're awake now. Take the jar before my apprentice sees it and quits on me.'
'I've got two weeks before the passes cl: 'I've got two weeks before the passes close. Walk the survey ridge first, then the long line up to the cartograph table. I'll mark what you bring back.'
'I've worked this quarry twelve years. T: 'I've worked this quarry twelve years. This rock isn't copper, isn't tin, isn't iron. It's heavier than it should be. Pull a sample and tell me I'm not losing my eyes.'
'Inner ring's got a walker in heavy plat: 'Inner ring's got a walker in heavy plate. Old, slow, but he's tall and he doesn't tire. Foragers won't go past the second tree. End it.'
'It's real. It's big. And it knows we're: 'It's real. It's big. And it knows we're hunting it.' She closes her log. 'Winteredge has the deep water. If we want it, we go where it lives.'
'Jorvik went out at first light and didn: 'Jorvik went out at first light and didn't tag the post. He's never late. Run the trail end to end, the loop's an hour if you push.'
'Last shift heard the rock groan three t: 'Last shift heard the rock groan three times in an hour. I'm not sending fifteen men down there blind. Take a pick and tell me what's pulling.'
'Lead smith took a fever. The pour's set: 'Lead smith took a fever. The pour's set for tomorrow and the mold doesn't keep. I need hands that don't shake at a heavy ladle. Eight bars, all platinum.'
'March in two weeks, full kit. Half my r: 'March in two weeks, full kit. Half my runners can't go three hours. You'll set the pace and they'll keep it or quit. Either's fine.'
'Maren Hask. Forty years brewing, never: 'Maren Hask. Forty years brewing, never sick a day. Found at the bottom of her cellar steps with a broken bottle in her hand. We're calling it an accident. I'm not.'
'My boy came back at midnight with frost: 'My boy came back at midnight with frostbit ears and no sled. Gnolls. Whole pack of them down off the ridge. Take one. I just want them to know we're still here.'
'My charts blew off the deck two nights: 'My charts blew off the deck two nights back. Walk the seaside, mark where the crabs are running, and come tell me before sunrise.'
'My contract says forty crates by Sunday: 'My contract says forty crates by Sunday. I've got twelve. The bigger fish only run at the deep lake and my back's gone. Take my rods.'
'My cousins. Right. I knew it before you: 'My cousins. Right. I knew it before you walked in. I needed it on paper. Thank you for that.'
'My good net snagged a rock and the line: 'My good net snagged a rock and the line snapped clean. It's down off the seaside somewhere. Pull what you can and bring me a few fish to prove the net still works.'
'My old notes drift a finger every year. Five years on, the cartograph's wrong by a hand. I need someone with steady feet to redo the survey before the guild reprints.'
'My rival's out on a job until Friday. H: 'My rival's out on a job until Friday. His stash is in the old hideout off the survey road. Empty it, we split, and don't leave a body.'
'Nets shredded three nights running. I s: 'Nets shredded three nights running. I saw it once at dusk, low and long and not afraid of me. Bring me the head and I'll believe you.'
'New shaft hit something dense at sixty: 'New shaft hit something dense at sixty feet. I want the first three loads pulled by someone who isn't on my payroll. You're it.'
'No fire near the arc. The bridge mistak: 'No fire near the arc. The bridge mistakes heat for a pulse and we lose a week of tuning. Cut it down with a blade or come back tomorrow.'
'No fire, no spores in the arc. Clean wo: 'No fire, no spores in the arc. Clean work. Take the lamp and don't tell the apprentices what was under the bridge.'
'No one's charted the pinnacle in eleven: 'No one's charted the pinnacle in eleven years. Last man who tried came down a finger short. You climb, I'll mark.'
'Old bard says you'll do, and from him t: 'Old bard says you'll do, and from him that's a parade. Booking ran out tonight but the next one is yours if you want it. Pay's same, take the tip jar.'
'One down. Hideout pays. If the thaw bri: 'One down. Hideout pays. If the thaw brings up another we'll send for you again.'
'Oven hand quit at noon. I've got a coun: 'Oven hand quit at noon. I've got a council feast at sundown and four hours of bake time and nobody who can keep the hearth steady. You. Now. Apron's on the hook.'
'Pack pulled back? Good. They'll go arou: 'Pack pulled back? Good. They'll go around us next time. My boy will sleep tonight. Take what you carry, and tell the campfire keeper I said put your tab on me.'
'Patrols come back in two days, half of: 'Patrols come back in two days, half of them frostbitten and the other half drunk. I need a batch ready or they'll drink the wrong cask. Help me brew it right.'
'Patrols ride out Monday and they drink: 'Patrols ride out Monday and they drink serene like water in the cold. I need forty bottles by Sunday and my apprentice quit on me. You up for it?'
'Pinewrap will have heat by morning. I'd: 'Pinewrap will have heat by morning. I'd have done it myself in three days. You did it in three hours. Take the bound stock. I owe you a favor I'll remember.'
'Pot went dry, stew's on the bottom blac: 'Pot went dry, stew's on the bottom black as char. Six regulars come in an hour. Get the hearth going and cook something they'll eat.'
'Rains shifted half my markers. I need t: 'Rains shifted half my markers. I need the survey line walked before the field claims start. Reset the stakes where the slope took them.'
'Real ground. Real lines. The expedition: 'Real ground. Real lines. The expedition leaves on this map next week. Pay's already in the box behind you.'
'Rebind held first try. That hasn't happ: 'Rebind held first try. That hasn't happened in nine years. Your signature goes in the log. Take this and don't come back unless I send for you.'
'Redhelm. The lieutenant works out of th: 'Redhelm. The lieutenant works out of there. I can't send my people that far. You'll need to finish this yourself.'
'Road stays open. The merchant's family: 'Road stays open. The merchant's family will hear about it tonight. There's a chest in the back you've earned. Don't argue the size of it.'
'Road's still open. Take this and don't: 'Road's still open. Take this and don't tell my sister I paid full price. She'd skin me.'
'Roots gone, ledge clear, morning shift: 'Roots gone, ledge clear, morning shift on schedule. That's the kind of work that gets you on the long list. Take this and don't share where you got it.'
'Rows nine through fourteen went brown i: 'Rows nine through fourteen went brown in one night. No frost, no rot smell. I want every leaf turned and the soil scraped before I lose the rest.'
'Salt merchant doubled his price overnig: 'Salt merchant doubled his price overnight. If I pay it I lose the season. Go work him down. Bring two pounds back at half what he's asking or don't bring anything.'
'Second verse fell out of my head halfwa: 'Second verse fell out of my head halfway through. Pit went quiet, mother in the front row went red. Sing it with me before the bell.'
'Shadeshore's letter came two hours befo: 'Shadeshore's letter came two hours before the thing breached off our seaside. Big as a skiff, dark on top. Took out a buoy line. We need eyes on it before we lose another boat.'
'Shortening. We thought so. Don't tell t: 'Shortening. We thought so. Don't tell the apprentices. They're scared enough of the rift already.'

'Six bars short. Buyer arrives by dusk. I need someone on the foundry while my apprentice runs the mine. Move.'
'Six potions, all standing. That's a wee: 'Six potions, all standing. That's a week's work in a night. Take the bonus and a bed. Don't argue.'
'Six varieties grow in the high canopy t: 'Six varieties grow in the high canopy that I've never seen below the line. Frost takes them in a week. Bring me one of each.'

'Sixty plates, no returns. The bride's m: 'Sixty plates, no returns. The bride's mother sent these for whoever saved us. She didn't ask which apron, so I'm giving them to yours.'
'Smith took it without a word. That's as: 'Smith took it without a word. That's as close to thanks as you'll get from him. Here's yours.'
'Smithy's intact, wall's not. We'll trad: 'Smithy's intact, wall's not. We'll trade the wall. Captain signs off. Pay's in the box.'
'Smugglers are moving goods through my a: 'Smugglers are moving goods through my alley after dark. They've cut into my trade three weeks running. Find out who they answer to.'
'So I wasn't mad. Good. Smith says I nee: 'So I wasn't mad. Good. Smith says I need a bigger forge. Riverwatch keeps the old foundry records. Try them next.'
'Some scrap of a kid dipped my belt at t: 'Some scrap of a kid dipped my belt at the bar last night. Purse had my whole week in it. Walk the alley, find the kid, take it back. No knives.'
'Something's been singing in the crypt u: 'Something's been singing in the crypt under the chapel since the moon turned. Two apprentices walked down to listen and didn't walk back up. End it.'
'South row's gone black at the base. Pul: 'South row's gone black at the base. Pull clean stems from the orchard before the rot jumps the path. Don't touch the leaves on the way through.'
'Spit's smoking through fish faster than: 'Spit's smoking through fish faster than the boats land them. Run the sea line, work the lake, then bring the hauls back through the spit.'
'Stores are light and the cold's coming: 'Stores are light and the cold's coming early. I need deep-water catch, not pond scrap. Take a boat out past the breakers and don't come back with perch.'
'Summit and storm. Two notes. Bring both: 'Summit and storm. Two notes. Bring both home.'
'Tall one's down. Rest will scatter insi: 'Tall one's down. Rest will scatter inside a week. The supply runs go back to schedule Monday. Take this and the trail master's mark.'
'Thaw came early. Something walked out o: 'Thaw came early. Something walked out of the ice with it. Two of ours went looking and one came back. Finish it before the rest of the ice melts.'
'Thaw line moves a foot a day until it d: 'Thaw line moves a foot a day until it doesn't. I need it on paper before it locks. Two markers, one circuit, back by dark.'
'The arc shorted two nights ago. The lin: 'The arc shorted two nights ago. The lines into Pinewrap are cold. The font's still good. I need someone steady to feed it while I patch the run.'
'The arc's drifted a finger's width west: 'The arc's drifted a finger's width west. Doesn't sound like much. It's the difference between a sealed bind and a leak. We rebind tonight.'
'The arc's off by a full step. Run the f: 'The arc's off by a full step. Run the font for the base note, the conduit for the middle, and the arc for the high. Get them in line by tonight.'
'The dancers leave on the early caravan: 'The dancers leave on the early caravan and three sashes aren't spun. Pull silk from my patch and spin them at the studio. No knots.'
'The foundry's burning again? Then you'l: 'The foundry's burning again? Then you'll want the master's blueprint. He sealed it in the Ironice vault before he died. Nobody's opened that vault in a hundred years.'
'The hum is steady. The eclipse will pas: 'The hum is steady. The eclipse will pass over it without taking anything. You did this in half the time my last apprentice managed. Keep the bound stock.'
'The obelisk has hummed every dawn for n: 'The obelisk has hummed every dawn for nine years. Two weeks ago it stopped. The conduit downhill is still drawing, so the line isn't broken. Walk it with me. Tell me what you hear.'
'The obelisk runs down a little every ec: 'The obelisk runs down a little every eclipse. If it goes dark it takes a year to wake. I need bright essence pulled and channelled by tomorrow night.'
'The obelisk's been silent four nights r: 'The obelisk's been silent four nights running. Nothing's broken on the stone, so the silence is the message. Go read it.'
'The opening bard broke his hand last we: 'The opening bard broke his hand last week. Three nights, full set, court rules. You can read music or you can leave.'
'The rift sings the wrong key. Tune both: 'The rift sings the wrong key. Tune both ends and sit a seal on it.'

'The Stone Empress sleeps beyond the rif: 'The Stone Empress sleeps beyond the rift. We need her seal broken first. Cartograph the runes, then drag her out and end it.'
'The vault crew rotates at the third bel: 'The vault crew rotates at the third bell. You get one hour. Three crates, marked with a red thumb. Don't open them and don't slow down.'
'The vines came in with last winter's wi: 'The vines came in with last winter's wind and never died. Pull what the list says. Leave the saplings alone.'
'The Worldtree falters. Walk the three g: 'The Worldtree falters. Walk the three groves and bring back its heart.'
'There's a plant on the ledge approach t: 'There's a plant on the ledge approach that's grown roots through three ore carts. My crew can't get past it. I want it dead before the morning shift.'
'They cleaned the trays. That's the firs: 'They cleaned the trays. That's the first time this month. You're welcome back any shift.'
'Third caravan in a month. They take the: 'Third caravan in a month. They take the grain and leave the drivers walking. I'm out of guards and out of patience. Ride with the next run.'
'Third wheel this month, same axle. Some: 'Third wheel this month, same axle. Someone is loosening the pin and I'm losing contracts over it.'
'Three boats came in this week with fish: 'Three boats came in this week with fish no one on the dock recognizes. The deep run is bringing up things that shouldn't be near the surface. Bring me one, cooked, so we know it's safe.'
'Three cells. One under each town. Hit t: 'Three cells. One under each town. Hit them in order or he disappears for ten years.'
'Three days in one. Forester renewed. Yo: 'Three days in one. Forester renewed. You earned a permanent slot on the rotation. Pay's better than mine and I'm the one with the desk. Sign here.'
'Three days my drawer's come up light. S: 'Three days my drawer's come up light. Same shortfall, same hour. Work my stall a shift and tell me whose coin doesn't ring right.'
'Three dignitaries from the lowlands arr: 'Three dignitaries from the lowlands arrive Sunday. They've heard about our canopy songs. I won't have them leave thinking we're savages with lutes.'
'Three full houses. The court's not hand: 'Three full houses. The court's not handing out compliments, but they paid the full bond. That's the compliment.'
'Three names, one boat, no council. That: 'Three names, one boat, no council. That's clean. The fence pays in full and asks nothing else of you.'
'Three notes, one cycle. That's how it's: 'Three notes, one cycle. That's how it's supposed to sound. Don't let the scholars touch it for a week.'
'Three supply runs hit in two weeks. Sam: 'Three supply runs hit in two weeks. Same crew every time, one lizardman taller than the others doing the cutting. End him and the rest scatter.'
'Three weeks the till's been short. Same: 'Three weeks the till's been short. Same amount, same day. I want an outsider walking the stalls. Half the merchants here are my cousins.'
'Three weeks. The smith stopped writing: 'Three weeks. The smith stopped writing letters and started writing names. Mine's first on the list. Get it done.'
'Tomas took the green skiff out before s: 'Tomas took the green skiff out before sunrise. It's noon and the tide's been wrong all morning. Walk the seaside, see what's washed in.'
'Trial season's three weeks out. I need: 'Trial season's three weeks out. I need the circuit run end-to-end and every weak board flagged. Don't half-step it. The trials will catch what you miss.'
'Tube fell off the saddle somewhere betw: 'Tube fell off the saddle somewhere between the survey post and here. Three days of work on those sheets. Patron sees an empty desk and I'm done.'
'Tunnel dropped on Garric. We'll have hi: 'Tunnel dropped on Garric. We'll have him out by dusk. Go down the vein and pull samples off the new seam so the day isn't a loss.'
'Twelve dispatches in three weeks. All s: 'Twelve dispatches in three weeks. All signed for at this counter. None reached the recipient. My couriers swear they handed them to the carrier. The carrier swears the bags were sealed.'
'Twice the size. The tracker doesn't exa: 'Twice the size. The tracker doesn't exaggerate.' She rolls the report and seals it. 'Woodwater needs to hear this. I'll send a runner. You go ahead.'
'Two carts and change. Quota's met. Ther: 'Two carts and change. Quota's met. There's a wider chamber down there now, isn't there. We'll talk after the audit.'
'Two coast fishers gone this week. Both: 'Two coast fishers gone this week. Both at dusk, both with the same marks on the throat. Take it tonight. Don't let it feed a third time.'
'Two crates a week off the docks for a m: 'Two crates a week off the docks for a month. Council's about to ask questions we can't answer. Find the inside crew before they do.'
'Two of my runners blew their knees in a: 'Two of my runners blew their knees in a week. Post is three days behind. You walk fast? Good. Take the bag, hit the trail, don't open the sealed letters.'
'Two patches in a day. That's the best w: 'Two patches in a day. That's the best work we've had this season. Take the supplies and the bonus.'
'Wall's cracked from the yard to the bre: 'Wall's cracked from the yard to the brewery. Whatever did it is still on the grounds. Smithy's a quarter mile out and it's heading that way.'
'Wards on the old crypt fade a hair ever: 'Wards on the old crypt fade a hair every winter. The lich woke once already and we paid for it. I'd rather pay you now than the town later.'
'We lost two students to that thing alre: 'We lost two students to that thing already. It sits at the crystal and watches. The third student who tried to flee was found facing the wrong way. Find it and end it.'
'We're paying for ground truth. The last: 'We're paying for ground truth. The last scout drew us a coastline from a tavern. Walk the trail, mark the prospect, check the grove. Then come back.'
'We've had three nights of cookfires on: 'We've had three nights of cookfires on the western ridge. Goblins. Find their camp and burn what they can't carry off. Move before they pick a target.'
'Wet blade. Quiet crypt. That'll hold an: 'Wet blade. Quiet crypt. That'll hold another decade if we mind the font. Take this. The court master left it for you. She likes how you handled the blade.'
'Whole week's brew tastes like a barn fl: 'Whole week's brew tastes like a barn floor. One cask did it. Scrub the cauldrons, start a clean batch, and don't reuse a stave.'
'Winter buyers pay double and they're th: 'Winter buyers pay double and they're three weeks out. I need cured fur and hide before they come. The shallow wilds are picked clean. Go deeper.'
'Winteredge needs ledgers, salt, lamp oi: 'Winteredge needs ledgers, salt, lamp oil. Long route. Take it.'
'You and I both thought we'd swept it cl: 'You and I both thought we'd swept it clean. A wagon left my alley last week paying in fish coin. Cropshore coin. There's still a piece of it out there.'

He came out of the back room swinging a: He came out of the back room swinging a hauler's hook. He's down. The torn ledger pages were stuffed in his coat. The chandler stamped seals for a single buyer for two years.
He closes the chapel registry on both na: He closes the chapel registry on both names without comment. 'Two stones in the courtyard by spring. Lich is done. Take this.'
He copies the time twice and signs both. 'Under target on a cold week. The pass closes in five days. I'll print this as the standing record until the spring run.'
He counts coin onto the counter and slid: He counts coin onto the counter and slides a sealed envelope on top. 'Bonus from the cargo's owners. They asked who you were. I told them I didn't know. That's how it stays.'
He counts coin without looking up. 'Beac: He counts coin without looking up. 'Beacon trick. I'll have my boats carry one each from now on. The season's saved. The wreck stays where it is. Some of my crew's grandfathers are aboard.'
He counts coins onto the counter and sha: He counts coins onto the counter and shakes his head. 'You sang the line and let me keep the show. Take this and never tell my mother.'
He counts coins onto the table without l: He counts coins onto the table without looking up. 'They're staying another week. That verse you borrowed, return it. The grove keeper's owed a bottle.'
He counts gold onto the counter without: He counts gold onto the counter without looking up. 'You taught my crew the cleavage trick. That's worth more than the slabs. Don't be a stranger.'
He counts the bars onto the table and sl: He counts the bars onto the table and slides half across. 'Six men. A shift's pull. I owe you more than coin but coin's what I have.'
He counts the recovered crates onto the: He counts the recovered crates onto the dock and exhales. 'Four days of bread became a season. Take what you need from the long stores. You earned it twice over.'
He counts them twice and slides one back: He counts them twice and slides one back. 'That one's yours. If you see the boy, tell him his tools are out on the road for the next thief.'
He cuts down the alley with a sack of fa: He cuts down the alley with a sack of false coin and a punch. You don't take him in, you take the punch. Without it he's just another walker on the row.
He didn't stop writing when you came in. He spoke between lines, calm as a tutor correcting a student. You took his hand off at the wrist and the rest of him after. The five remaining names go free. The work he was building dies on the page.
He drops his knife on the bench. 'Knew i: He drops his knife on the bench. 'Knew it. Wife said I was drunk. Nets are safe, you're paid, and I'm telling this story for ten years.'
He fought like he had time to spare. The: He fought like he had time to spare. The seal cracks when he falls. Whatever held the chain together breaks with it.
He fought the way old men fight, slowly: He fought the way old men fight, slowly and without waste. The curtains came down in the second pass and the first sun came in and he aged four hundred years between one breath and the next.
He goes still. 'Stacked, not dumped. Som: He goes still. 'Stacked, not dumped. Someone meant my orchard. I'll find out who. You saved the canopy. Take the orchard's thanks in produce.'
He hands you the lead smith's apron, fol: He hands you the lead smith's apron, folded. 'Wash it before you give it back. Pay's in the purse. Lead smith owes you a drink when he's upright.'
He hands you the smaller auger and a scr: He hands you the smaller auger and a scrap of paper with names on it. 'Five kids in the village want to learn. Start with the one whose name is twice.'
He has a singed lockbox and a list of st: He has a singed lockbox and a list of stolen tools. 'Four shops hit this week. Scorch marks at every entry. Imps, plural. Find their nest and end the coven.'
He has a tooth on the counter the size o: He has a tooth on the counter the size of his thumb. 'Gnolls in the old number-three shaft. Pulled it last night from a timber. New dig starts in three days. Clear them.'
He hefts the punch and laughs once. 'Old: He hefts the punch and laughs once. 'Old trick. He'll buy fish honest next week or he won't eat. Take a stack for the shift and one for the catch.'
He keeps his hat low. 'The lizardman cre: He keeps his hat low. 'The lizardman crew moves three crates a week through my sting. I'm the fence in name. Cut the chain and they collapse. I'll feed you the timing.'
He laughs once and then looks at your no: He laughs once and then looks at your notes. 'Fine. I'll square it before the assessor arrives. Don't tell the clerk it was me.' You tell her anyway.
He logs the kill, signs it twice, and sl: He logs the kill, signs it twice, and slides the purse across. 'Three fishers spared. Two avenged. That's the work.'
He looks at the chip and looks away. 'I: He looks at the chip and looks away. 'I don't know the man. I know who pays for the wax. Redhelm chandler, works out of the prospect cabin. He stamps for anyone with coin.'
He nods at the new saplings and pours tw: He nods at the new saplings and pours two cups of cider. 'Six rows is bad. Twelve would have broken me. Take this and the rest of the cider.'
He pays in coin and a sack of fresh-cut: He pays in coin and a sack of fresh-cut ore from the new dig's test holes. 'The crew starts in three days. You bought us a clean shaft. Don't be a stranger.'
He picks a spot by the colour of the ice: He picks a spot by the colour of the ice, not the depth. 'Black ice means deep, white ice means thin, blue ice means lucky. Today we want blue.'
He pours flour from a measuring cup into: He pours flour from a measuring cup into a purse and slides it over. 'Council ate every crumb. Apron's yours if you want it. Pay's better than the wilds.'
He pours one of the new bottles for hims: He pours one of the new bottles for himself and one for you. 'First sip is for the brewer. Second sip is for the help. Drink.'
He pours two glasses without looking up. 'I sign pacts with people who can move goods quietly. Find the warehouse my cousin lost last spring. Then we talk terms.'
He puts a coil of cut net rope on the co: He puts a coil of cut net rope on the counter. 'Three boats this month. Something off the deep wreck is dragging them under. We won't crew the run until it's cleared.'
He reads the offsets and grunts. 'Five p: He reads the offsets and grunts. 'Five paces south. Same every spring. Field claims will hold now. Take this, I owe you the walk back.'
He reads the sample twice. 'Mithril, thi: He reads the sample twice. 'Mithril, this clean? You bought my crew six months of paid work. Take this and don't tell anyone where it came from.'
He reads your count, signs the pact, and: He reads your count, signs the pact, and hands you the wax-sealed copy. 'My houses will know your name by morning. So will the people I want them to know about.'
He returns the four shops' tools by hand: He returns the four shops' tools by hand the same evening. 'I'll keep the binding-dust trick in mind. You did the constable's work for him tonight. Eat at any of the four shops on the house.'
He rises when you enter and offers his h: He rises when you enter and offers his hand the old way, palm flat and turned aside. 'I served the house. I did not serve him. I have an old contract I would like released before its other party finds it.'
He sets a blackened branch on the counte: He sets a blackened branch on the counter. The bark sloughs off in your hand. 'Three south rows already. If it reaches the canopy I lose the orchard. Walk it with me.'
He sits by the fire for the first time y: He sits by the fire for the first time you have seen him sit anywhere. 'He taught me to read. He gave me my name. I have been waiting four hundred years to ask him to stop.'
He sniffs the pot and exhales. 'Saved my: He sniffs the pot and exhales. 'Saved my coat. The innkeep would've taken it for what I burnt. Take a stack and the inn's thanks.'
He spreads the contract on the sitting r: He spreads the contract on the sitting room table and runs a finger along the older signature. 'He is not bound to a place. He is bound to a debt. You cannot break the debt. You can answer it for him.'
He stands when you enter and inclines hi: He stands when you enter and inclines his head. 'I had hoped this could be settled by letter. I see it cannot. I will not be using my chair again.'
He stood seven feet and fought like he'd: He stood seven feet and fought like he'd done it a hundred times. He had. He hadn't done it a hundred and one. The banner comes down with him and the camp goes quiet.
He stops at the door and turns to the ha: He stops at the door and turns to the harbormaster. 'My business with this town is concluded. I am going to find a quiet country and finish a book I started a long time ago. Thank you both. Truly.' He bows once and is gone before morning.
He turns the bar over in both hands and: He turns the bar over in both hands and laughs once, dry. 'I told them my seam was strange. Nobody listened. Keep the bar. You earned it twice over.'
He walks beside you without speaking. Th: He walks beside you without speaking. The snow holds his weight but leaves no print. At the second turn he says, very quietly, 'He was kind once. I want you to know that before you meet him.'
He walks the circuit once before he pays: He walks the circuit once before he pays. 'Boards set straight, ropes doubled. You did it right. The trial crew will keep their teeth thanks to you.'
He walks you out past the bend where the: He walks you out past the bend where the lake floor drops twenty fathoms. 'Bait sinks slow, fish rise slow. Patient.'
He was already awake when you stepped in: He was already awake when you stepped into the chamber. He inclined his head the way the old houses do and said only, 'Thank you for coming yourself.' It was over before the second torch guttered.
He was slow but he hit hard. The plate s: He was slow but he hit hard. The plate split at the third strike and the rest of him followed. Whatever runes were on the bones are dead now too.
He weighs a sample in one hand and grins: He weighs a sample in one hand and grins. 'Garric's breathing, the seam's iron, the shaft's dry. Worst day of the month just turned. Here.'
He weighs each chunk and grunts. 'Good. The shaft's worth what I said it was. Take this and don't go telling the buyer my price.'
He weighs the haul and grunts. 'That'll: He weighs the haul and grunts. 'That'll do. Winter doesn't kill us this year. Your share's in the chest.'
He went down hard. The cargo is yours to: He went down hard. The cargo is yours to deal with later. One cell down.
He won't speak the whole way to the bank: He won't speak the whole way to the bank. The clerk takes one look at him and sends a runner south. 'Your aunt'll be at the southbank by morning. She'll want to see you on your feet.'
He's already at the counter with two aug: He's already at the counter with two augers and a sled. 'I've taught the lake for forty years. Walk a circuit with me, and you'll teach the next lot when I'm gone.'
He's at the same shingle, same boat. You: He's at the same shingle, same boat. You hand him double what he asked. He pockets it without counting. 'Knew you'd be back. Most aren't.'
He's tucked behind crates near the south: He's tucked behind crates near the south door. The coat's still folded under his arm. He gives it back without a swing. You give him the mark anyway.

It came apart in three pieces and seeded: It came apart in three pieces and seeded the air with one last burst. You held the cloth and waited it out. The bridge didn't catch a single ember.
It came at you from the south snowbank,: It came at you from the south snowbank, jaws first. The spear held. The pack scattered into the white when their lead went down.
It came out fast and low like he said. Y: It came out fast and low like he said. You took a bite on the boot for it. The thing's bigger than two normal rats stitched together. Head's intact.
It came out of the wall like it remember: It came out of the wall like it remembered being there. You break it apart and the corridor goes quiet. The seal at the next door is still cold.
It came through halfway before you close: It came through halfway before you closed with it. You finished it standing astride the seal. The crack ran black for a moment, then sealed clean under the demon's weight.
It came through the hairline before you: It came through the hairline before you finished the seal lines. Three swings and a clean stamp on its forehead. It tries to barter on the way down. You don't answer.
It came through to test the disc. The di: It came through to test the disc. The disc held the rift, not the herald. You finished the herald yourself. One enforcer down before the main contract holder shows.
It came up between two barrels with one: It came up between two barrels with one arm. You finish it before it finds the second. The cook's salted hams are intact. Mostly.
It came up out of the bank slow and went: It came up out of the bank slow and went down fast once you got the angle right. The water clears within an hour. Whatever it was carrying went into the runoff.
It came up out of the cold patch with a: It came up out of the cold patch with a rusted plowshare in one hand. You take it apart at the joints. The marks on the trees stop glowing once it falls.
It comes up through the stage in a colum: It comes up through the stage in a column of cold air. It's been waiting for the anthem since the anthem was written. You put it down before it reaches the second row.
It fought hard. The roots kept moving fo: It fought hard. The roots kept moving for two minutes after the stalk went down. You burned the stump for good measure. The ledge is clear.
It fought like a sailor who didn't know: It fought like a sailor who didn't know it was dead. You took it apart on the deck and threw the remains back over. The water under the boat goes warm again within minutes.
It met you on the lip of the crater with: It met you on the lip of the crater with a contract folder under one arm. It opened with terms. You answered with the bound blade. The pact ended on the first swing. The rest of the fight was an old thing that already knew it was over, refusing to admit it.
It saw you in three directions at once a: It saw you in three directions at once and still went down. Whatever it was watching for, it didn't see you coming the way it expected.
It takes six of you on the cable and fou: It takes six of you on the cable and four hours of pulling. The thing comes up dead from the depth change, longer than the boat shed, dark blue and grey. It is a fish. Just one nothing was supposed to bring up.
It turned the wall into a crater before: It turned the wall into a crater before it dropped. Took longer than you wanted. The smithy's still standing, which is the only number that mattered.
It was waiting in a hollow a quarter-mil: It was waiting in a hollow a quarter-mile south, half-curled around its own heat. You closed under the steadying draught and finished it before it could step back through the rift. The body cooled by the time you walked away.

She came in calm and left swinging a hoo: She came in calm and left swinging a hooked blade. Now she's on her own carpet. The seal on her finger matches the one from Longha.
She closes the missing-student ledger an: She closes the missing-student ledger and pours two cups. 'Two students dead, one orbiter ended. That's a bad ledger but it stops bleeding. Take this.'
She copies the marks onto fresh paper an: She copies the marks onto fresh paper and pours you a mug. 'Three runs is more than I'd hoped. Tide's at four. Take this for your trouble.'
She counts forty-two and adds two for th: She counts forty-two and adds two for the trouble. 'Caravan's saved. New anvil's coming by ship. You worked while I sat, take what's fair.'
She counts the bundles, signs the roll,: She counts the bundles, signs the roll, and pays you in coin from a tin that says CONTINGENCY in chalk. 'Same time next year. Don't tell the corner booth I tipped you.'
She counts the crates twice and writes y: She counts the crates twice and writes you a tab at the inn. 'Forty-one. I owe you a real drink the day my back stops aching.'
She counts the purse twice. 'Twelve minu: She counts the purse twice. 'Twelve minutes to spare and three crates clean. That's the cleanest lift this quarter. Take your cut.'
She counts them under lamplight. 'Thirty: She counts them under lamplight. 'Thirty even. Caravan won't know the smith was hurt. You saved a contract and his pride. Take this.'
She crosses herself and unbolts the back: She crosses herself and unbolts the back door. 'Old chapel runs under us, didn't think anything was left in it. Take the lamp and the wage, both earned.'
She doesn't look up from her notes. 'My: She doesn't look up from her notes. 'My team broke through a wall four nights ago. The chamber on the other side isn't on any of my maps. I need someone steady to walk in with me.'
She doesn't smile. She does sit down. 'T: She doesn't smile. She does sit down. 'Twelve days. We'll be ready. The Highroot singer can keep the fee I would have paid you. You did the harder work.'
She drinks and nods slowly. 'That's our: She drinks and nods slowly. 'That's our brew. I was ready to dump the season. You bought it back. Take a case home, the customers won't miss it.'
She has a foraging knife on the counter: She has a foraging knife on the counter that isn't hers. 'Two of my pickers came back without their hauls. One didn't come back. Find the band and end it.'
She has a score with one line scratched: She has a score with one line scratched out and three in its place, none of them right. 'The third harmony is wrong. The autumn anthem opens in twelve days. Fix it.'
She has melted footprints in a folded oi: She has melted footprints in a folded oilcloth. 'Stepped right out of the survey ground at dawn. The trail went south and the snow boiled where it set down. Find it and close the rift.'
She has the full slate now, six verses a: She has the full slate now, six verses across two pages. 'The amphitheatre's been booked and I traded a month of court work for the slot. If it goes the way the old book says, nobody in the front rows leaves the same.'
She has the pot at a hard boil already. The crabs go in without ceremony. She times the second one off the chapel bell up the lane.
She has three fires going and an oven yo: She has three fires going and an oven you could fit a sheep in. 'Roast goes on now. While it cooks you'll fetch me one thing from the vein.'
She lays the three maps side by side and: She lays the three maps side by side and traces the ridge with a finger. 'You doubled my range and saved me a season. Take your pay and the cold-weather coat.'
She lays them out, runs her thumb along: She lays them out, runs her thumb along every seam, and nods once. 'Captain pays me on delivery. You get yours up front. Don't say I never gave you a fair shake.'
She lets out a breath she's been holding: She lets out a breath she's been holding for a week. 'I'll write down who came through. I'll know their name before the month ends.'
She listens without interrupting. 'A tap: She listens without interrupting. 'A tap from the other side. I'll log it and write the council. You bought us a clean line this week. That's enough for now.'
She listens, sets down the wax stamp, an: She listens, sets down the wax stamp, and walks out without a word. Through the window you see her cross the square toward the inn. He's still at the back table.
She locks her case and hands you the sla: She locks her case and hands you the slate. 'You've got the lyric. I've got the line. If the back row hears it, the front row feels it. If the stage feels it, the piece does its work.'
She met you at the door in a maid's apro: She met you at the door in a maid's apron and didn't speak. She fought like she'd been doing it for thirty years and didn't remember any of them. You ended her on the threshold.
She passes the lockbox to a woman behind: She passes the lockbox to a woman behind the spice stall. Three crates of dyed cloth change hands. You lift the box when she steps away.
She pays in coin, a wheel of sharp chees: She pays in coin, a wheel of sharp cheese, and a sealed jar of her own salt blend. 'You can run my second oven any time. Don't forget the recipe was mine.'
She pays in winter prices though winter: She pays in winter prices though winter hasn't started. 'Buyers paid up front. You're getting paid up front. That's how this works when nobody's cheating.'
She placed second and looks happier than: She placed second and looks happier than the winner. 'My crab was better. The judge's brother runs the stall that beat me.'
She pours two drinks and slides one acro: She pours two drinks and slides one across. 'My grandmother knew. She wrote the sixth verse short on purpose. Said the piece was a key, and a key only fits one lock.'
She pulls a bottle of whiskey from under: She pulls a bottle of whiskey from under the counter and pours two. 'Both our marks held. I'll check it every dawn for a month. Drink, then go sleep.'
She reads the contract and folds it care: She reads the contract and folds it carefully. 'He has been here longer than my grandfather's grandfather. If he says the binding can be released, I believe him. Help him finish it. Please.'
She reads the letter twice. 'My people a: She reads the letter twice. 'My people are at the underground entrance now. We go in the moment you're ready.'
She rolls a half-finished map between he: She rolls a half-finished map between her fingers. 'Four scouts, three weeks overdue. I want the maps back, the scouts if they're standing. Walk the route they took.'
She rolls the sheet, seals it, and stows: She rolls the sheet, seals it, and stows it in the chest behind her. 'That cavern's worth a second trip in spring. Snow'll bury the entrance by week's end.'
She seals the rubbing in oilcloth and po: She seals the rubbing in oilcloth and pours two cups of cold tea. 'The script names a place across the veil. I'll need to read more before we go further. Come back when I send word.'
She slides three burnt conduits across t: She slides three burnt conduits across the counter. 'These went in fresh last week. They came out like this. Something downline is pulling more than it should.'
She splits the guild payment in half and: She splits the guild payment in half and slides one half across. 'That's your share. Workshop keeps its seal. You ever want a bench, it's yours.'
She struck the moment you reached for th: She struck the moment you reached for the door. The fight was short and ugly. She is dead at the threshold. You can hear the Empress breathing in the chamber.
She thumbs every page twice. 'Six variet: She thumbs every page twice. 'Six varieties, all named, all dated. That's a year's work in a week. Take this for the climb alone.'
She traces the gaps with one finger. 'An: She traces the gaps with one finger. 'Anchor, voice, return. Someone meant to cut the obelisk loose. Battlefrost uses the same three.'
She tunes a beat-up lute on the counter: She tunes a beat-up lute on the counter without looking up. 'I'm short a verse for a piece my grandmother used to play. Walk the expedition trail and see if anyone scratched the words anywhere.'
She turns each one in the light. 'These: She turns each one in the light. 'These will outlast the dancers. They always do. Take this and the festival's blessing.'
She turns the oar over twice. 'Tomas is: She turns the oar over twice. 'Tomas is on the south rocks, soaked but breathing. Whatever took his skiff, it wasn't a current. You did right bringing this in.'
She unrolls the sheet, looks at it for a: She unrolls the sheet, looks at it for a long minute, and pours you a cup of something that burns. 'Smoke past the western range. I'd ask what you saw, but I don't think either of us wants the answer.'
She unwraps the first cut and laughs onc: She unwraps the first cut and laughs once, short. 'Tomas's skiff was nothing to this. You took the thing that took his oar. Sit. Eat.'
She waits until her people are out of ea: She waits until her people are out of earshot. 'My sister's boy. Seventeen. He walked the Redhelm road four weeks back to see a girl. He hasn't come home. I'm not asking as a captain.'
She walks the rack twice and stops at th: She walks the rack twice and stops at the boar hide. 'Buyer won't haggle now. Quota's met. Take the offcuts, they're worth a coin in town.'
She walks the row at dawn and counts the: She walks the row at dawn and counts the same eight. 'That'll save the harvest. The rest I'll burn before it spreads. You earned this stack.'
She was faster than you expected and you: She was faster than you expected and you were faster than she expected. Throat first, then the heart. She unmade herself with a long breath.
She wraps the cuttings in waxed cloth. ': She wraps the cuttings in waxed cloth. 'You'll want to ride to Pinegap before the next rain. The archive's still there. The herbalist isn't, but the books might be.'
She writes it down twice. 'Outward, not: She writes it down twice. 'Outward, not in. Something out there's learned to drink. I'll watch it tonight. Here, you saved me a week's notes.'
She writes the readings down twice. 'Off: She writes the readings down twice. 'Offshore, deep, and old. We don't wake it. We just learn to listen back. You did good work.'
She's already drinking. 'The Drypocket p: She's already drinking. 'The Drypocket patch sent it our way. The court basement is open and someone's been signing in it. The names on the wax aren't all human.'
She's already wearing her apron at the c: She's already wearing her apron at the counter. 'Three towns sent cooks this year. I need crab and I need it before the judging bell.'
She's older than the camp and meaner tha: She's older than the camp and meaner than the weather. 'Crab from the spit, herbs off the patch, a song at the fire. You're the runner. I'm the cook. Don't bring me anything I didn't ask for.'

The arc takes what's left in one quiet p: The arc takes what's left in one quiet pulse. No smoke, no scream. The arc keeper closes the lid and locks it. 'Nothing comes back from this.'

The baker speaks without looking up from: The baker speaks without looking up from her dough. 'He came in every third day for a quarter loaf. Pale, polite, never sat down. He stopped coming the week the disappearances started. He had ink on his cuffs both hands.'
The bakery feeds the cast for free betwe: The bakery feeds the cast for free between shows. You eat with the lutenist. She tells you which verses the court actually likes. It's not the ones in the book.
The bakery is loud and hot. You run four: The bakery is loud and hot. You run four batches of loaves and two of rolls between the two working ovens. She tastes the first roll and grunts once. That's a pass.
The banker doesn't blink. 'Sealed since: The banker doesn't blink. 'Sealed since my grandfather's time. Nobody asked, nobody opened it. You want the key, you sign for what's inside before you see it.'
The banker hauls up a crate from the bac: The banker hauls up a crate from the back. 'These came in with her apprentice when he came home alone. The reduction recipe's in the second jar from the top.'
The banker locks the oilcloth in a stron: The banker locks the oilcloth in a strongbox without asking what's inside. 'Henrik doesn't need to know. You don't need to know either. Take the coin and forget the colour of it.'
The banker stacks crates against the bac: The banker stacks crates against the back wall. 'Picks, files, dust masks, three weeks of food. Whatever you don't take, I keep. Whatever you bring back, I weigh.'
The banker stamps the registry and slide: The banker stamps the registry and slides a copy back to you. 'Yours, by the signature. The original stays here. Whatever you forge from it, you forged from scratch.'
The banker wraps the bottles in straw an: The banker wraps the bottles in straw and ties the crate. 'Lastlight's cauldron runs hot. Don't let it boil twice. The apprentice's last note said it cracked the first jar.'

The bard hums a stanza you know. The sam: The bard hums a stanza you know. The same key as the pact.

The bard seals the new measurements in a: The bard seals the new measurements in a tube. 'The treants won't speak to strangers. Take these to their council at Stillbark and don't rush them. They keep their own time.'
The bard tunes three pipes to the leaves: The bard tunes three pipes to the leaves and sings the old line. The canopy answers a full beat late. 'That's the wrong answer. The roots aren't keeping time.'
The bards at the court know three songs: The bards at the court know three songs about the canopy. Two are warnings. The third is a name. They sing it quietly and look at you when they finish.

The orbiters don't turn. They've been po: The orbiters don't turn. They've been pointed at the chamber for so long they can't look away. You walk past them on the lee side and they don't notice. Good.
The bellows are still hot. You smelt the: The bellows are still hot. You smelt the ore he set out and stack the bars on the cooling rack. Ten clean ingots, not a slag among them.
The bench is laid out the way she left i: The bench is laid out the way she left it. Her crafting kit is half done, a saddle strap pinned mid-stitch. You take fresh cord and her good knife. The dust is exactly seven days deep.
The bench-keeper exhales when she sees h: The bench-keeper exhales when she sees him. 'Slow, not dying, fine. You ran the loop he couldn't. Take his pouch, he'll moan less about owing you.'
The blight runs in straight lines, not i: The blight runs in straight lines, not in patches. Whatever's spreading it has a path, not a wind. The grovekeeper marks the worst trees with chalk as you go.
The blueprint calls for a slow quench in: The blueprint calls for a slow quench in still water, not the foundry trough. You walk the bar to the field's runoff pool and watch it hiss for a long minute. It rings true when you tap it.
The boss came at the door with a hook in: The boss came at the door with a hook in one hand and the boy by the collar in the other. He didn't get to use either. The boy is shaking but uncut.
The boss looks at the pelt and nods once: The boss looks at the pelt and nods once. 'They won't be back this season. Eat. We move north in the morning.'
The bottleneck held. The leader hit the: The bottleneck held. The leader hit the choke first and hardest, with the rest of the pack stacked behind it. You took them one at a time as they pushed through. They won't be back this winter.
The bowyer has a strong recurve already: The bowyer has a strong recurve already strung. 'Take it. Pay me when the warband is done. My cousin was the picker who didn't come back.' He hands you a quiver without making eye contact.
The boy is tangled with the wrong crew i: The boy is tangled with the wrong crew in Redhelm. Get him out alive.
The breach is wider than the captain sai: The breach is wider than the captain said. Stone the size of a cart. The tracks past it are slow and even. Whatever's making them isn't running.
The Brew skill lets you enhance potions: The Brew skill lets you enhance potions with materials for stronger effects.

The brewer hands you a corked bottle of: The brewer hands you a corked bottle of something that smells like pine and honey. 'Two swallows before the second verse, one before the fifth. You'll thank me when you hit the high line.'
The brewer lays out the ratios in chalk: The brewer lays out the ratios in chalk on the bench. 'Three to one. Two passes. Skim after the first, or we'll lose half to the foam.'
The brewer reads the slip and frowns. 'T: The brewer reads the slip and frowns. 'That's my hand. I sold Maren a draught of pale draught last month. She told me it was for a buyer who wanted strong sleep. The buyer signed off as her apprentice.'

The brewery is warm and the kettles alre: The brewery is warm and the kettles already lit. You pull the serene blend in steady passes and the brewer counts forty bottles by the third kettle.
The brown rows trace a perfect line, not: The brown rows trace a perfect line, not a patch. Something walked the path between rows eight and nine and the trees on the wrong side died of it.
The cairn is half-buried in old ice. You: The cairn is half-buried in old ice. You touch the top stone and the boss's second runner calls the time from a hundred yards back. You're under his target by a full minute.
The camp boss spits into the snow. 'They: The camp boss spits into the snow. 'They circled us three nights running. Cook's bow is short. We need the lead gnoll down or we don't sleep again.'

The campfire bends to it. The wind quiet: The campfire bends to it. The wind quiets, listens, then howls back.

The captain marks the route on the map. The raid is broken.
The captain pays the ferry and waves you: The captain pays the ferry and waves you off. 'Redhelm's the last cell. Whatever's left of him will be there.'

The cartograph crew has the lich's chamb: The cartograph crew has the lich's chamber under Glowrock now. The lead surveyor signs the chart and gives it to you. He does not say goodbye. None of them do.
The cartograph crew records the seal tim: The cartograph crew records the seal time in the margin and dates it. The lead surveyor adds a second line under it. 'Will hold a season. Maybe two.'
The cartograph crew strikes the chamber: The cartograph crew strikes the chamber line off the chart. They write the date under it. The lead surveyor pours a glass and sets it on the table for the archaeologist. She isn't there yet.
The cartograph table has three sheets fo: The cartograph table has three sheets for the hollows and none of them agree. The forager picks the oldest and taps a circle near the centre. 'This is where it was when I was a girl. Start there.'
The cartographer checks your load four t: The cartographer checks your load four times. 'No second trip. Whatever you forget here, you summit without.' She signs the flag pole over to you.
The cartographer reads the case in silen: The cartographer reads the case in silence. 'These maps reach further north than anyone has charted. I'll send a proper team for the other two. You did the part I needed.'
The cartographer wakes long enough to st: The cartographer wakes long enough to stamp the maps and slide them into the locked drawer. 'Pole's two weeks out. You're coming with us when we go.'

The trade master unrolls the charter on: The trade master unrolls the charter on a barrel head. 'Five seals. One per town. Bring them all back here and we open a market the syndicates can't touch.'
The trader slides the ledger across. 'Fi: The trader slides the ledger across. 'Five towns, five deals, walked in order; the book's yours if you close them all. Stray and the prices stop matching the page.'
The trail boss has a stopwatch and a cre: The trail boss has a stopwatch and a creased map. 'Snow's a week out. I need the summit run timed in fair weather before it closes. You're the legs I have on hand.'
The trail crosses into Ridgetop's foragi: The trail crosses into Ridgetop's foraging den. Their fire is still warm, the stew still in the pot. Six raiders, maybe seven. You count their packs and circle wide.
The trail forks twice where the old map: The trail forks twice where the old map shows one fork. You mark both and walk the eastern split until you can see the prospect line below.
The trail is long and dry. You set a pac: The trail is long and dry. You set a pace the old runners would have called showy. Your knees agree. The bag is half its weight by the third drop.
The trail is older than the warband's. L: The trail is older than the warband's. Long stride. Deep claw. The grove animals are gone in a wide circle. You follow the empty quiet uphill.
The trail is wide enough for three abrea: The trail is wide enough for three abreast. They aren't hiding. You count cookfire pits at every rest stop. Big eaters.
The trail runs through churned bracken a: The trail runs through churned bracken and a felled cart. Lizardmen don't bother with cover. They expected to win every fight on this road and so far they have.
The traps in the pool are still heavy. Y: The traps in the pool are still heavy. You haul up enough for the table and a pot besides.
The tube is wedged under a thornbush dow: The tube is wedged under a thornbush downhill of the post. The wax cap held. The sheets inside are still crisp and the inkwork hasn't run.
The tunnel under the market opens into a: The tunnel under the market opens into a vault of stolen cargo. Two dozen runners and a captain on a chair of crates. They don't run.
The upper pack came down the ridge again: The upper pack came down the ridge against the wind. You took the big one at the rope step. The rest didn't follow.
The upper vein runs clean for ten feet t: The upper vein runs clean for ten feet then twists east. Whatever's pulling on the rock is deeper down.
The vampire in the inner court was the l: The vampire in the inner court was the lich's last lieutenant. She steps aside when she sees the chart in your hand. 'I have been waiting for the one who would close the door. Make it fast.'
The vault is colder than the street. You: The vault is colder than the street. You find the three red-thumbed crates stacked against the back wall. They're heavier than they look.
The Veilbridge arc has drifted out of tr: The Veilbridge arc has drifted out of true and the binder wants it walked back into alignment.
The Veilbridge rift hasn't closed for ni: The Veilbridge rift hasn't closed for nine days. The bridge wardens are out of options.
The vein gives up half a cart of mithril: The vein gives up half a cart of mithril before the rock turns to slag. You scratch a line on the wall to mark where the next crew should start.
The vein here is honest titanium, nothin: The vein here is honest titanium, nothing more. You strip enough to pay for the expedition and keep moving. The deeper readings still point east.
The vein's been worked half-blind this s: The vein's been worked half-blind this season. You pull enough clean rock to fill a barrow and roll it back through the dust.
The venture office has eyes along the ro: The venture office has eyes along the road. The map gets a fresh mark every hour. Two pack camps. One on the high cut, one on the river bend. The river bend is the soft one.
The venture route is the dangerous desce: The venture route is the dangerous descent. You take it at three-quarters pace and still close out the run with breath to spare. The marker post at the bottom is fresh-painted for the timing run.
The vines come up easy once you get unde: The vines come up easy once you get under them. Three sacks before the light goes. The saplings underneath are starting to push through again.
The vines have the same black rind under: The vines have the same black rind under the leaves. Whatever it is, it crossed the lane in under a week. You bag two cuttings and a strip of bark.
The wagonmaster counts the sacks twice. 'All twenty. First clean run all month. The trade master at the bank wants a word with you when you've a moment.'
The ward-tender feeds you imbue charge i: The ward-tender feeds you imbue charge in steady doses while you re-pour the seal lines. The font holds. 'Whoever drew the circle that fed this rift is still out there. Glowrock, probably. Check the court.'
The ward-tender hasn't slept in two days: The ward-tender hasn't slept in two days. 'The font's down a third. Something split the seal at the crystal and I can't patch it alone. I need a body who can hold a line.'
The ward-tender meets you with the seal: The ward-tender meets you with the seal lines half re-poured. 'It split again the day after Glowrock burned. Same hairline. Whatever you cut over there had a parent. The court ledger pointed at Sootstep. So do my lines.'
The ward-tender pours the new seal lines: The ward-tender pours the new seal lines herself this time. The font runs clean for the first time since Glowrock. 'No more hairlines. No more debtors at the crystal. Whatever you did at Sootstep, the contract on this town is closed. Sit down. You look terrible.'
The warden has lost two men in two days. 'The pack you cleared on the road. Their leader didn't run. He went up. Whatever was leading him is still up there. It's older than any of them.'
The warden sets a bundle of bark shaving: The warden sets a bundle of bark shavings on the counter. 'Tomb under the south root has been humming for nine nights. Same tone every dusk. We sealed it a century back. Nothing in there should still have a voice.'
The warden signs the contract without re: The warden signs the contract without reading it. 'Two men this week. None next. That's how I'll measure it.'
The warden takes off his hat and wipes t: The warden takes off his hat and wipes the sweat off his neck. 'Foragers go back tomorrow. Take this. Whatever runes were on him are mine to bury.'
The warehouse is hidden behind a stand o: The warehouse is hidden behind a stand of dry hedgerow. Inside: six crates, a ledger written in the same hand as the lieutenant's, and a side door that opens onto the road.
The watch captain is waiting. 'We've had: The watch captain is waiting. 'We've had eyes on the crater since you left. He's there. We can hold the road but we can't go in. You'll need to be the one who walks through that door.'
The watch captain spreads a smudged map: The watch captain spreads a smudged map on the counter. 'Raiding party of fifteen, maybe twenty. They came down through the crater two days ago and they're not slowing down.'
The water past the breakers is black and: The water past the breakers is black and slow. Lines run deep here. You hook three fish in a row that wouldn't fit in the smaller harbor's nets.
The water's wrong here. Cold patches whe: The water's wrong here. Cold patches where the sun should warm it. Your line pulls and pulls and then snaps. Whatever's down there moved off west.
The waves run sideways for fifty yards n: The waves run sideways for fifty yards near the shore, not in, not out. The same pull. Whatever it is, it sits offshore and listens.
The weapon is destroyed. The gems used t: The weapon is destroyed. The gems used to upgrade it are returned to the bank.
The weather effects in Settings let you: The weather effects in Settings let you toggle snow, desert heat, and day/night cycles per zone.
The wheel runs smooth. You spin three sa: The wheel runs smooth. You spin three sashes in the colors she pinned to the board, knot the ends the way the eldest dancer likes.
The wilds accept it. Smaller, but the sa: The wilds accept it. Smaller, but the same line.
The wilds give willingly. The Worldtree: The wilds give willingly. The Worldtree is in every leaf.
The wilds open onto the long sightline a: The wilds open onto the long sightline at the old marker stone. The new fix lines up clean with the survey ridge. You mark the stone with chalk for the next walker.
The wilds thin out into bare rock fifty: The wilds thin out into bare rock fifty paces in. You find the orbiter hanging in the air over a dry pool, watching its own reflection. It hasn't blinked.
The wind off the ridge cuts your fingers: The wind off the ridge cuts your fingers half-numb in twenty minutes. You pencil in the fossil bed, three burrows, and a passage that wasn't on last year's sheet.
The Winteredge harbormaster lays out a c: The Winteredge harbormaster lays out a chart weighted with stones. 'Abyss shelf is six miles out. We rig the heavy lines from the coast. Three boats, four lines each. You take the lead.'
The wood splits clean. The totem holds.
The Woodwater harbormaster opens the col: The Woodwater harbormaster opens the cold crate and doesn't say anything for a long time. 'My dock ate fish for a month off this. Tell your harbormaster the debt's noted.'
The work at Ridgemill was practice. The: The work at Ridgemill was practice. The lich behind it is finishing the real thing at Glowrock.
The workbench shop was hit last night. T: The workbench shop was hit last night. The good chisels are gone, the apprentice's stipend is gone, and one window is cracked outward, not inward. They left through the window in a hurry.
The workshop benches are crowded. You ta: The workshop benches are crowded. You take a corner and work through the order one piece at a time. The cuts are clean once you get the rhythm.
The workshop crafter holds the thread up: The workshop crafter holds the thread up to the lamp. 'That's not from anything I know. Not blight, not rot. It came up from below.'
The workshop crafter trims and stretches: The workshop crafter trims and stretches the hides for you, takes half a stack for the favor, and points at the curing rack. 'Come back in the morning.'
The workshop crew sorts the sacks fast. 'Good cut. Whoever's been doing this the last month has been pulling root and all. It kills the next growth too.'
The workshop racks are warm. You stretch: The workshop racks are warm. You stretch the skins out, salt them, and hang them between the older pieces so they cure the same color.
The workshop's old map matches the marke: The workshop's old map matches the marker exactly. The grove had a second stand half a mile north and no one alive remembered it.
The world is shrouded in fog of war — wa: The world is shrouded in fog of war — walk the map to clear permanent vision around your path.
Their boat sits low in the water. You ma: Their boat sits low in the water. You mark the hull with the fence's chalk so the dock crew finds it at dawn. It'll never leave the inlet.
Their bound enforcer woke up the moment: Their bound enforcer woke up the moment you opened the door. You ended it before it could reach the contracts. The contracts go in your bag.
Their cache is half the missing caravans: Their cache is half the missing caravans, packed and ready to move deeper. You burn what you can't carry. Smoke goes up over the canopy for an hour.
Their captain came over the log swinging: Their captain came over the log swinging a two-handed axe and screaming. He stops doing both. The rest scatter into the trees without him.
Their enforcer was no man. It had been b: Their enforcer was no man. It had been bound to the cell by old contracts. You broke the contract and the binding with the same blade.
Their muscle came up swinging. He's down: Their muscle came up swinging. He's down. The runners scatter and the guard captain's people sweep up the rest.
Their pack leader stood and fought inste: Their pack leader stood and fought instead of running. You cut him down at the cut mouth. The road past the mine is open.
They had been laying behind a stack of c: They had been laying behind a stack of clay pots in the back corner. Forty-two eggs, most still good. The farmer counts them twice and shakes your hand without smiling.
They listen without interrupting and the: They listen without interrupting and then write the ending into the third song. One of them slides a copy across to you. 'Most never come back to give us the last verse. We thank you for ours.'
They were waiting on the same barge that: They were waiting on the same barge that came in this morning. Neither of them ran. The fence in Longha will sleep easier when the word reaches him. So will the clerk.
They were waiting where the road narrows: They were waiting where the road narrows past the orchard line. Hired muscle, syndicate coin. You drop the captain and the rest scatter into the trees.
They will be kicked after the rename so: They will be kicked after the rename so the new name takes effect immediately.
They've made a kill point at the mine cu: They've made a kill point at the mine cut where the road narrows. You go in from above and they don't see you until the third one is already down. The rest break and run for the camp.

Three coats' worth of hide laid out, mar: Three coats' worth of hide laid out, marked, and cut clean by lamp's end. Your shoulders are stiff but the pieces stack on her stitch table without a flaw.
Three hauls warming at once. The conduit: Three hauls warming at once. The conduit hums and holds. The harbour crew start carrying barrels off the dock before you've finished tying up.
Three hides short. You find them on the: Three hides short. You find them on the back trail an hour out. The previous crafter cached them and never came back. You take what you need.
Three sets a night for four nights, and: Three sets a night for four nights, and the room fills by the second song. The old bard sits in the corner with his sling and corrects your timing twice. Both times he's right.
Three sheep in the back paddock, all dry: Three sheep in the back paddock, all dry as paper. The cuts on their necks are clean and small. The farmer says she's losing one a fortnight and nobody she's told will come look.

You and the smith work the plate in alte: You and the smith work the plate in alternating strikes. The pattern comes out clean on the third heat. The smith stamps her own mark next to yours. 'Now it's both of ours.'

You arrange your kit. The crater air sme: You arrange your kit. The crater air smells of cinder.
You bank the coals and scrape the trays: You bank the coals and scrape the trays while the head baker counts coppers behind the counter. She nods once. From her, that's a parade.
You bind a beacon to a marker buoy and c: You bind a beacon to a marker buoy and charge it at the conduit. Dropped over the wreck, it will hold light against the haunt long enough to put it down.
You bind fresh shafts and re-set two hea: You bind fresh shafts and re-set two heads that came loose in the cold. The crafter hands you a flask. 'For the walk back. Whichever way it goes.'
You bind saplings and cuttings. The grai: You bind saplings and cuttings. The grain still hums.
You bring in a hold of fish on the first: You bring in a hold of fish on the first cast of the new water. The spit cook fillets one and grills it on the spot. 'Cleanest fish off that wreck in fifteen years.'
You bring the root to the warden and rea: You bring the root to the warden and read him the re-cut verse. He grinds the wrong line off the obelisk with his own hand and speaks the true name. The humming dims by the third word and is gone by the seventh.
You burn the slip tying the stash to the: You burn the slip tying the stash to the fence. The cauldron eats it without smoke. By morning nobody will prove a thing.
You buy small, sell small, take notes. T: You buy small, sell small, take notes. The fish stall undercounts coins. The grain stall overcounts. Two of the other stalls do both depending on the buyer.
You came down the rope in the middle of: You came down the rope in the middle of their fire pit. The fight was the loudest five minutes of your year. The high cut is yours. The road is open all the way south.
You can adjust the map quality in Settin: You can adjust the map quality in Settings to improve performance on slower devices.
