You can drag the edges of the chat panel: You can drag the edges of the chat panel to resize it.
You can now end a queued combat while yo: You can now end a queued combat while you are still walking to the mob, instead of having to wait until you arrive
You can now leave or end a Fortress from: You can now leave or end a Fortress from inside the raid
You can now name your raid lobby, and th: You can now name your raid lobby, and the Raid tab opens straight to the lobby browser
You can now save materials even when an: You can now save materials even when an action fails
You can pin quests to the quest tracker: You can pin quests to the quest tracker for at-a-glance progress while skilling.
You climb to the ledge and the deep sent: You climb to the ledge and the deep sentinel turns to meet you. The fight is short. The ledge is yours and the vein is open above it.
You collect what came off without distur: You collect what came off without disturbing the stand. The dragonhide is fresh enough to still smell of the animal. You leave a marker rock so the next surveyor knows where to look in the spring.
You crouch in the patch and pull hawk se: You crouch in the patch and pull hawk seed and calm bloom the way she showed you. The roots come up clean. You shake the dirt off and wrap them in the cloth from her apron.
You cut a counter-sigil at the fragment: You cut a counter-sigil at the fragment and bind it to the conduit master's mark. The next pull from the other side meets resistance. The tap closes by inches.
You cut and burn the dead wood and plant: You cut and burn the dead wood and plant six new saplings. The new soil holds. Whatever walked the path is gone for now.
You cut back the worst three rows to cle: You cut back the worst three rows to clean wood and burn the trimmings on the headland. The grovekeeper salts the stumps. By evening the chalk marks come off easily.
You cut the leather to her chalk lines a: You cut the leather to her chalk lines and stitch through the night. By the third pair your fingers stop hurting. By the eighth they hurt worse.
You cut the sigil onto two fresh wax dis: You cut the sigil onto two fresh wax discs while the clerk reads the name from the second ledger out loud. The discs warm in your hand. They'll hold once, against the one they were cut for.
You drag the last two roped miners clear: You drag the last two roped miners clear, then work the seam fast while the slab still holds. The shift's pull is saved as the roof comes down behind you.
You drive the stake in past the last pat: You drive the stake in past the last patch of bare ground. The ice creaks under your boot. You walk the line south and keep the rope taut.
You drive the ward stakes at three point: You drive the ward stakes at three points along the grove. They won't stop another warband but they'll buy the caravan guards a warning. That's enough for now.
You drop back one camp to top the sigils: You drop back one camp to top the sigils up at the font. The cartographer says nothing while you work. Both of you know the weather window is shrinking.
You drop into Farnorth on the leeward si: You drop into Farnorth on the leeward side of the ridge. Half the team is already digging out a wind shelter. The cartographer hasn't slept in two days.
You drop the cave's location with a bard: You drop the cave's location with a bard at the Highroot court. By morning, the warden's people are picking the remaining four out of the back of the cave one by one. The cargo goes back to its owners by afternoon.
You drop the heavy line where the den tr: You drop the heavy line where the den tracker said the dead one washed up. Something hits it once, hard enough to drag you a step. Then it lets go.
You drop two of the rotten props at the: You drop two of the rotten props at the entry chamber to bottle the chamber and force a single approach. The pack hears the timbers fall and moves toward the noise. Good.
You feed bright into the font in steady: You feed bright into the font in steady draws. The ward stitches itself back firm. The hum in the keeper's bones eases. She nods you on toward the crypt.
You feed the font the final reading. The: You feed the font the final reading. The binding closes around the chamber and seals the corridor behind you. The chamber is a grave now. It will stay one.
You feed the rift the full reading. The: You feed the rift the full reading. The seal pulls taut across the chamber. The breathing slows. It does not stop. 'Long enough,' the archaeologist writes in the margin. 'Not enough.'
You feed the rift the threshold lines an: You feed the rift the threshold lines and three of the new ones from the cartograph. It locks. The first anchor will hold the seal in place while you re-tie the rest.
You find his path along the inner ring,: You find his path along the inner ring, deep prints in the moss where the plate weighs him down. Two old swords lie where he dropped them and didn't notice.
You find the first stake leaning, the se: You find the first stake leaning, the second buried, the third still upright. The line wants to wander south by five paces. You straighten it with rope and a level.
You gut and salt the haul on the spit so: You gut and salt the haul on the spit so it'll keep the ride back to Sandscale. The smell pulls a stray cat. It earns a tail.
You hack two straight stems from the plo: You hack two straight stems from the plot and bind them with the strap off your pack. The brace holds his ankle when he tries his weight on it.
You haggle with the stubborn merchants a: You haggle with the stubborn merchants and come away with favorable terms. The trade master will be pleased.
You haul the worst of the larder out to: You haul the worst of the larder out to the snow plot and burn it on a downwind fire. The smell carries west, away from the new dig. The shaft is breathable again by evening.
You have been banned. Appeal to the mods: You have been banned. Appeal to the mods in the Discord. Hopefully this is just a misunderstanding and we can help you easy!
You help heave sacks onto two flatbed wa: You help heave sacks onto two flatbed wagons. The wagonmaster checks the axles twice and mutters about the bend past the orchard line.
You hold the new ore beside fresh titani: You hold the new ore beside fresh titanium from the upper vein. The new one weighs half what it should. The miner spits on the floor and crosses himself. 'Whatever that is, it's not for digging.'
You hold the syrup at a slow simmer for: You hold the syrup at a slow simmer for an hour. It darkens to the color the brewer wanted on the first try. The hearth keeper nods once.
You ink the spring in at the cartograph: You ink the spring in at the cartograph table while the cartographer measures distances with a string. The cavern mouth above it lines up with a star on her older chart.
You lay the dust across the threshold an: You lay the dust across the threshold and tear down the boards. The chattering stops. Six imps and one bigger one stare back at you from inside. The big one moves first.
You let him talk for a full minute, poin: You let him talk for a full minute, point out the cracked sacks at the back of his stall, and walk away once. He calls you back. Two pounds. Half price.
You now auto-eat food during raids, the: You now auto-eat food during raids, the same as in normal combat
You pace the ridge above the expedition: You pace the ridge above the expedition cairn and log three new bearings. The cartographer writes them in on the master chart. One bearing was wrong by half a mile.
You pack the heart for the long walk hom: You pack the heart for the long walk home.
You pick six leaves from six heights, th: You pick six leaves from six heights, the way the bard's notes ask for. Two of them are the wrong colour underneath. She'll want to see that.
You pick up the seal kit.
You place the bundle at the orchard's ce: You place the bundle at the orchard's centre. A second treant steps forward, slow as a season. 'The shape is correct. The wood is correct. We accept the agreement.'
You press the chart against the chamber: You press the chart against the chamber stone. The seal takes. The door eases shut a finger's width, then another. The Empress speaks once, behind the stone. Two words. You don't translate them.
You put a palm flat to the stone. It's w: You put a palm flat to the stone. It's warm, the way a man's chest is warm, and you can feel something underneath it that should be a hum and is instead a slow, off-time tap.
You read it out at six-eight to the cour: You read it out at six-eight to the court master. He stops mid-pour and listens. 'That's a hill march. Bring it back to her in the right time and she'll know it.'
You read the chart back into the rift on: You read the chart back into the rift one more time. The first anchor holds. You feel it settle. The lich knows you are coming now. There is no quiet way left.
You read the lich's name from the chart: You read the lich's name from the chart into the rift. The rift resists, then takes. The first anchor is set. It will hold for as long as you are standing.
You read the release. The anchors fall a: You read the release. The anchors fall away one at a time. The rift closes around the silence and stays closed. The threshold is a wall again. The veil is the veil again.
You roll the totem in cloth and start th: You roll the totem in cloth and start the climb.
You run the team through the arrest dril: You run the team through the arrest drill until the slowest climber can stop a fall in under two seconds. The cartographer calls it good and pulls the ropes in.
You salt the pot, work the fire down, an: You salt the pot, work the fire down, and turn out enough fish to fill six bowls. Smells better than whatever he was making.
You scatter a line of seed from the gard: You scatter a line of seed from the garden toward the greenhouse and crouch behind the fence. The lead goose stares at you for a long time. Then she eats the seed.
You sell a basket of dried fish and a co: You sell a basket of dried fish and a coil of rope. Around the third bell, a regular pays in two stacks. The bottom coin in one stack rings dead.
You serve a thin winter broth, no garnis: You serve a thin winter broth, no garnish. The judge eats the whole bowl, slides his list across with every dish checked and the last one underlined.
You set the cartograph table on the lowe: You set the cartograph table on the lower bluff and shoot lines at three peaks while the light holds. The middle peak isn't where last year's chart says it should be.
You set the charge into the rift's edge: You set the charge into the rift's edge and trip it. The tear sucks closed in a single beat. The surveyor's marker poles sing for a second from the pressure change, then go still.
You set the jar in a pot of water and br: You set the jar in a pot of water and bring it slow. The eels stop moving around the time the lid starts rattling. You keep the lid on.
You set the new boards and run the upper: You set the new boards and run the upper rope twice over. The pit holds your weight at sprint. It'll hold a trial team.
You set the plate into the fragment hous: You set the plate into the fragment housing. The fragment flares once and pulls the binding tight. Then a hand comes through the hairline before it can close.
You set the sigil chain along the rope. The font takes the charge slow in the cold. The cartographer nods when the last stone settles. 'They'll hold a week.'
You set the team for the last pitch in t: You set the team for the last pitch in the yard's lee. The cartographer hands you the flag. 'I get us up. You plant it. That's the deal.'
You sing the two lines at marching tempo: You sing the two lines at marching tempo. She mouths the third before you start it. 'That's the one. There are more verses out there. One per region.'
You sink the hooks past the shelf. The c: You sink the hooks past the shelf. The cables go slack in cold deep water. The crew on the shore waits. Nothing for an hour.
You sit by the fire long enough to thaw: You sit by the fire long enough to thaw the laces on your boots. The trapper's boy points out the ridge where the sled went over. You can see the pack tracks from here.
You speak at the last arc, one word. The: You speak at the last arc, one word. The whole circuit catches the note and holds it. The keeper finds you sitting against the conduit, listening.
You stack the pyre on the open trail and: You stack the pyre on the open trail and set it. The smoke goes straight up. Whatever held the canopy quiet for a hundred years is gone with it.
You stamp the writ. The boats are waitin: You stamp the writ. The boats are waiting.
You stand on the cap stone for the count: You stand on the cap stone for the count of forty. You can see the inland sea, three valleys, and a column of smoke past the western range.
You stay off the main trails. The traps: You stay off the main trails. The traps the tanner pre-set are heavy with deer and one boar that fought the rope. Plenty of weight for the rack.
You stepped into the cave mouth as the l: You stepped into the cave mouth as the leader came out for air. The fight was short and ugly. The other four broke for the back of the cave and you let them go. The leader was the chain. He's broken.
You stoke, vent, rotate, and pull for th: You stoke, vent, rotate, and pull for three straight hours. The breads come out the color of dark honey. The head baker doesn't speak. That's good, here.
You strike the stone in even passes. By: You strike the stone in even passes. By the last cut the obelisk has started humming under your hand. The note settles and holds.
You strike the stone with the keeper's b: You strike the stone with the keeper's brass rod three times. The first two go dead. The third sets the obelisk humming for a count of nine, then back to the slow tap. Something's answering, just not all of it.
You strip the camp for anything useful a: You strip the camp for anything useful and burn the rest. The smoke rolls down into the hollows. Anyone within a mile knows the warband is finished.
You strip the pack, dry the maps over th: You strip the pack, dry the maps over the yard brazier, and roll them tight. The wax holds the snow off through the night.
You take her seal pattern to a back-room: You take her seal pattern to a back-room crafter. He copies it onto fresh wax in twenty minutes and pockets the gold. 'Don't use it twice in one week.'
You take stems from the older trees firs: You take stems from the older trees first, the way she showed you. The bark is dry, the cuts heal pale. None of them carry the rot.
You take the court's verses, not the boo: You take the court's verses, not the book's. The hall claps once at the end, then a second time, slower. The lutenist doesn't say I told you so.
You take the new growth and leave anythi: You take the new growth and leave anything that touched the bad cask. The plot smells right again as soon as the old basket goes on the fire.
You took the leader at the fire pit with: You took the leader at the fire pit with one shot from the recurve and finished the rest at close range. The packs hold the picker's haul and his knife. They were going to sell it back to the warden.
You wait out the hours by the fire on th: You wait out the hours by the fire on the cliff above the estate. He'll be weakest in the first hour of full light and he knows that as well as you do.
You wait until the carrier ties up. A wo: You wait until the carrier ties up. A woman in a dyer's apron slips out, lifts the satchel, ducks back inside. She's out again in fifteen minutes with the bag resealed. She doesn't see you in the rain.
You walk her route again with fresh iron: You walk her route again with fresh iron pins and set the next season's markers yourself. The grove holds its breath while you work. When you finish it lets it out.
You walk the cleared face. The seam runs: You walk the cleared face. The seam runs another forty yards into the cliff. The foreman will have his crew back on it before the week ends.
You walk the floor for an afternoon. Thr: You walk the floor for an afternoon. Three stalls overcharge, one undercuts to dump bad stock, and one barters straight. You write each down in the clerk's book.
You walk the last unmapped section befor: You walk the last unmapped section before the col. The line goes up a sixty-degree slab and across a knife ridge to the cairn. There is no second option.
You walk the line node by node. The draw: You walk the line node by node. The draw spikes hardest at the third junction and runs cold past it. Whatever's pulling sits between here and the arc.
You walk the ridges with the compass and: You walk the ridges with the compass and the surveyor's old book. The drift shows up in three places, all small, all in the same direction. The guild map is leaning west.
You wrap her knife in oilcloth and lay h: You wrap her knife in oilcloth and lay her crafting kit out clean. The letter from her pack sits on top. Whoever she meant it for will come for it eventually.
You wrap the lit pact around a clean bla: You wrap the lit pact around a clean blade haft at the workbench. The glow climbs the blade. The clerk steps back. 'That'll only last one swing. Make it count. It will already know you're coming.'

Your hand on the stone gets nothing back: Your hand on the stone gets nothing back. Then, slow as a tide, the obelisk answers with a pulse so deep it sets your teeth ringing. It was listening, not sleeping.

Your line tugs hard twice and then goes: Your line tugs hard twice and then goes still. What comes up has too many eyes and the wrong color gills. It's heavy. You haul it across the rocks to the spit.

One fight, held still. A full tier 5 mel: One fight, held still. A full tier 5 melee kit at level 55 against a Savage Rat. Each side shows its combat skills on top and its gear stats underneath, the same as a live fight.
Your hit points are twice your Life skil: Your hit points are twice your Life skill. 55 Life is 110 HP. The rat has 109 Life, so 218 HP.
A dagger is a melee stab weapon. Of all: A dagger is a melee stab weapon. Of all these skills, only four matter for this attack: your Strike and Heft, and the rat's Dodge and Defend.
Accuracy skills on the left, strength sk: Accuracy skills on the left, strength skills on the right.
Your accuracy skill plus your stab attac: Your accuracy skill plus your stab attack makes one score. The rat's Dodge plus its stab defence makes the other. 215 against 137 gives an 83% chance to hit.
Strike 55 + Stab attack 94 = 215. Dodg: Strike 55 + Stab attack 94 = 215.   Dodge 66 + Stab defence 5 = 137.
If you hit, your strength skill plus you: If you hit, your strength skill plus your melee strength stat sets the max hit. Here that is 43, and the attack rolls between 1 and 43. Say it rolls 30.
The rat's Defend is flat damage reductio: The rat's Defend is flat damage reduction. 45 Defend removes 9% of the damage, so your 30 lands as 28.
Dodge decides if you hit. Defend decides: Dodge decides if you hit. Defend decides how much damage gets through.
Look at the rat's defence column. Crush: Look at the rat's defence column. Crush 87 and Magic 82 are high. Stab 5 and Range 3 are low. A dagger is strong here because the rat has low stab defence compared to its other defensive stats.
Every weapon attacks with one of five st: Every weapon attacks with one of five styles, and every target defends each of those five separately. Pick the style your target is weakest against.
The rat's stab defence is its lowest, so: The rat's stab defence is its lowest, so a dagger works well on it.
These two are different. Each one trains: These two are different. Each one trains and scales off its own school, but attacks a different defence.
To train ranged, use the bow. Against a: To train ranged, use the bow. Against a target with high ranged defence, switch to the crossbow. You keep the same ranged skills and bonuses, but attack their stab defence instead.
